money_at_stake.rationale: The occurrence is the Xi-Putin Bishkek talks on Power of Siberia 2 (SCO summit, Aug 31 2026), not a signed construction contract, so there is no official project cost to cite; Gazprom itself has not disclosed one. What is citable is a converging range of independent construction-cost estimates, $13.6bn to $34bn (Moscow Times, itself sourcing the low end from SCMP reporting and the high end from a Carnegie Politika analysis). The whole range sits inside B10_100 (comfortably above the $10bn floor, nowhere near $100bn), so the band is not sensitive to exactly where in that range the true figure lands. Capacity context (50 bcm/year, close to Nord Stream 1's 55 bcm/year design capacity, over a roughly 2,600km route through Mongolia) corroborates that this is a first-tier pipeline project and not a rounding error, without itself being a dollar figure.

evidence.claim: Independent estimates put the pipeline's construction cost between $13.6 billion and $34 billion, and Gazprom has disclosed neither an official cost nor a construction schedule.
evidence.source_name: The Moscow Times, What the Power of Siberia 2 Deal Really Means for Russia and China
source_excerpt: Estimates for the price tag range from $13.6 billion to $34 billion.
Moscow has yet to announce a construction schedule or its official cost.

evidence.claim: The pipeline is designed for 50 billion cubic metres per year of capacity (about 525 TWh), nearly matching Nord Stream 1's 55 bcm/year design capacity, running about 2,600km from western Siberia through Mongolia to China.
evidence.source_name: Al Jazeera, What is the Power of Siberia 2 pipeline that Russia, China are planning?
source_excerpt: Once built, the pipeline is expected to have a capacity of 50 billion cubic metres (1.77 trillion cubic feet) per year, equivalent to about 525 terawatt-hours of energy

The pipeline would be nearly as large as Nord Stream 1, one of Russia's most important former gas export routes to Europe, which had a design capacity of 55 billion cubic metres (1.94 trillion cubic feet) per year.
a proposed 2,600km (1,616-mile) natural gas pipeline that would carry Russian gas from western Siberia through Mongolia to China.

public_reach.rationale: Of the three evidence items in the prior version of this appraisal, two failed re-verification this run and are deleted rather than repaired: the GlobalSecurity.org/Sputnik item (naming CNPC, not PetroChina, as the Chinese signatory) returned HTTP 403 on every fetch attempt this session, including a Wayback Machine attempt this session's tools cannot even reach; the ngoreport.org item (TMK's OFAC SDN listing) returned no retrievable body on repeated fetch, only a truncation placeholder. What survives, fetched and quoted directly this run, is the Gazprom side: Gazprom's Western depositary-receipt programs were terminated in 2022 under Russian Federal Law 114-FZ (Gazprom instructed Bank of New York Mellon to terminate the deposit agreement on 29 April 2022, the same day notifying the UK Financial Conduct Authority of intent to delist from the London Stock Exchange), so a Western brokerage account cannot legally hold or trade Gazprom today. Gazprom is the Russian-side party that would carry the bulk of the pipeline's own capex (money_at_stake's own citation records that it is Moscow/Gazprom, not a listed operator, that has not disclosed the project's cost), which alone anchors this at the low end even without the now-uncitable claims about the Chinese counterparty's listing status or TMK's sanctions status. I have not myself verified a citable second-order listed set on either side of this deal this run; none is asserted here. Score held at 15, 'state, private, or sanctioned dominated', on a narrower evidentiary base than the prior version of this file.

evidence.claim: Citing Russian Federal Law 114-FZ, Gazprom directed Bank of New York Mellon on 29 April 2022 to terminate the depositary-receipt deposit agreement covering its shares, and the same day notified the UK Financial Conduct Authority of intent to cancel the London Stock Exchange listing and asked the London and Singapore exchanges to delist the receipts within 20 business days.
evidence.source_name: Gazprom, Termination of the Depositary Receipt Programmes in Relation to Shares in PJSC Gazprom
source_excerpt: In compliance with the Federal Law No. 114-FZ dated 16 April 2022... PJSC Gazprom is required to terminate its Deposit Agreement with The Bank of New York Mellon under which depositary receipts (the "DRs") representing shares in the Company are placed.
Today PJSC Gazprom instructed The Bank of New York Mellon to terminate the Deposit Agreement.
29 April 2022, when Gazprom notified the UK's Financial Conduct Authority of its intention to cancel the London Stock Exchange listing
asked the London Stock Exchange and the Singapore Exchange to delist its depositary receipts within 20 business days

capture_odds.rationale: Even setting reach aside, this does not look like a chain where money sticks as profit. The Eurasian Times item from the prior version of this appraisal (China's price framed as a third to half of Gazprom's European rate, plus a Putin quote) returned HTTP 403 on every fetch attempt this session and is deleted rather than repaired. What survives, fetched and quoted directly this run, is the Asia Times pricing breakdown: China has offered roughly $50/tcm against a Russian ask near $250/tcm, itself below the $240-280/tcm Power of Siberia 1 rate and well below the $275-340/tcm Gazprom charged Europe before the war, with no timeline for a deal in sight despite talks continuing. A seller with a weaker hand (sanctions, war financing pressure, Europe's LNG phase-out) facing a buyer opening at a household-subsidy-level price is a price-taker setup, closer to a commodity/regulated-return outcome than a margin-capture one, which is why this sits near the low anchor rather than the middle. Score held at 25 on this narrower evidentiary base.

evidence.claim: China's opening offer is about $50 per thousand cubic metres, versus Russia's ask near $250/tcm; by comparison Power of Siberia 1 currently prices at $240-280/tcm and Russia's earlier pipeline sales to Europe ran $275-340/tcm. No deal timeline is in sight even though neither side has walked away.
evidence.source_name: Asia Times, Power of Siberia 2 deadlock belies Russia-China 'no-limits' pact
source_excerpt: China is demanding that it be permitted to pay US$50 per thousand cubic meters, the heavily subsidized rate Russian households pay at home
Russia is asking for about US$250 per thousand cubic meters.
China already imports Russian gas via the Power of Siberia 1 pipeline at US$240 to US$280 per thousand cubic meters
Before the war in Ukraine broke out in February 2022, Russia sold gas to Europe and Turkey at US$275 to US$340 per thousand cubic meters.
Neither side has formally walked away, but no timeline for a deal or for construction to begin is in sight.

timing_fit.rationale: Measured against this occurrence's own anchor (the 2026-08-29 dated news of the 2026-08-31 Bishkek talks), the money is not committed inside the window. As of the most recent dated reporting fetched this run (Asia Times, mid-2026), neither side has formally walked away but no timeline for a deal or for construction to begin is in sight, with talks continuing only at the corporate (Gazprom-CNPC) level. The Bishkek and follow-on Eastern Economic Forum discussions (SCMP) are talks about talks, not a groundbreaking. Even in the fastest credible path (agreement reached at or shortly after Bishkek), a pipeline project of this scale would plausibly take several years to build once financing and pricing are actually settled: an analytical judgment, not a separately cited figure in this appraisal. Not scored at the bottom anchor because a real, high-level, calendar-dated event (the Bishkek meeting itself) is happening inside the window and could be the trigger that unblocks financing.

evidence.claim: As of mid-2026, neither side has formally walked away from the pipeline's negotiations, but no timeline for a deal or for construction to begin is in sight, with the Kremlin describing talks as continuing only at the corporate level.
evidence.source_name: Asia Times, Power of Siberia 2 deadlock belies Russia-China 'no-limits' pact
source_excerpt: Neither side has formally walked away, but no timeline for a deal or for construction to begin is in sight.
The Kremlin says talks continue at the corporate level.

evidence.claim: Xi and Putin are expected to meet bilaterally in Bishkek on Monday, August 31, during the SCO summit, to discuss the pipeline; Russian officials say it will also be raised at the Eastern Economic Forum in Vladivostok, held September 1 to 4.
evidence.source_name: South China Morning Post, Xi, Putin to meet in Bishkek for Power of Siberia 2 pipeline talks: Kremlin
source_excerpt: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian leader Vladimir Putin are expected to discuss the Power of Siberia 2 project in a meeting in Bishkek on Monday
The issue will be discussed bilaterally
It will be discussed not only at the level of the [September 1-4] Eastern Economic Forum [in Vladivostok], but also in the meeting with the Chinese leader, which will take place on August 31.
